audit_findings.title: The owner-earnings model may misclassify recoverable rate-base investment as maintenance consumption
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 PP&E additions were $185.1 million versus $88.7 million of depreciation and amortization, a computed $96.4 million excess; the recoverable or growth portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Deducting recoverable growth and infrastructure capital as maintenance capex depresses OE without including the associated future rate-base revenue and allowed return; it also makes growth amplify a negative anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Earnings from Unitil’s utility operations are derived from the return on investment in the five distribution utilities and Granite State.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification problem with valuation-scale consequences. The filing establishes that earnings are derived from returns on utility investment and that capital projects can receive base-rate, step-adjustment or tracker recovery. The $96.4 million excess of 2025 additions over depreciation is more than twelve times the $7.9 million OE loss, so even a modest reclassification could reverse the anchor and the scenario behavior. The record does not identify how much of the spending was true maintenance, so it demonstrates a material risk rather than a quantified error amount.
audit_findings.action: Classify 2025 and projected capital spending project by project as replacement maintenance, growth, mandated infrastructure or acquisition consideration; match recoverable projects to approved rate orders and trackers, then rebuild OE and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor is not a steady-state earnings numerator for the current perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 OE was negative $7.9 million after a $53.8 million reversal; FY2025 included $3.1 million of transaction costs, only $8.3 million of Maine Natural revenue and $2.8 million of Maine Natural net income, while first-half 2026 included $8.7 million of Maine Natural adjusted gross margin
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE reflects partial-year acquired operations and transaction costs, while the share denominator and balance-sheet context represent the enlarged company; perpetuating it understates the recurring numerator belonging to those shares.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 31, 2025, the Company acquired all issued and outstanding shares of Maine Natural for $ 86.0 million in cash, plus $ 7.1 million in working capital, subject to certain adjustments as provided in the Purchase Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. FY2025 included eleven months of Bangor and two months of Maine Natural, whereas the valuation uses July 2026 shares and June 2026 balance-sheet data. First-half 2026 results also show positive earnings and a full-period Maine Natural contribution, confirming that the negative FY2025 OE is not a like-for-like steady-state numerator. The exact normalized owner earnings remain unquantified because recurring capital requirements, acquisition financing and integration costs must still be separated.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a twelve-month pro forma OE bridge for Bangor and Maine Natural using recurring revenue, O&M, taxes, interest and normalized maintenance capex; exclude acquisition consideration and separately identify the $3.1 million of 2025 transaction costs, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter could omit the pending Aquarion transaction
audit_findings.magnitude: The June 30, 2026 acquisition used $42.6 million of cash consideration, added $62.0 million of net utility plant and $13.5 million of acquired long-term debt, with an additional $42.6 million acquisition-financing tranche outstanding
audit_findings.mechanism: The completed AWC-NH and Abenaki acquisition changes the operating OE perimeter, financing interest, debt context and capital requirements; a null perimeter leaves those operations out while the June balance sheet already includes the transaction.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate enterprise value of the sale is approximately $ 100.0 million, which includes approximately $ 70.0 million in cash and the assumption of approximately $ 30.0 million of debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves this from a possibility into a demonstrated perimeter error: Unitil acquired AWC-NH and Abenaki on June 30, 2026. No water revenue was recognized through that closing date, so the FY2025 anchor contains none of the acquired earnings, while the June balance sheet contains the acquired assets, debt and financing. The net value direction is mixed because operating earnings and rate-base returns add value, while interest, capital requirements and assumed debt reduce it. The transaction amounts are large relative to the modeled equity values of negative $75 million to negative $122 million.
audit_findings.action: Replace the null perimeter with the completed AWC-NH and Abenaki transaction; construct pro forma water OE including OTSA costs, maintenance capex and acquisition interest, and reconcile the acquisition financing, assumed debt, cash and shares before rerunning all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A fixed share denominator may not support the assumed capital program and growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $37.5 million remained under the ATM at June 30, 2026; at $53.71 per share that is a computed approximately 0.698 million shares, or 3.8% of the 18.254698 million valuation denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Future equity issuance increases the share denominator and reduces per-share value unless the funded investment produces sufficient incremental OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, $ 48.5 million remains available for future sales under the program.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing denominator substantially captures the current count: 18.236674 million shares were outstanding on July 31, compared with 18.254698 million fully diluted shares used. The remaining concern is forward-looking financing rather than a demonstrated current denominator error. Unitil already issued 212,042 ATM shares during the first half of 2026 and retains substantial ATM capacity, so dilution should be monitored as the capital program and acquisition financing develop.
audit_findings.action: Create a financing schedule for projected utility capex and acquisition refinancing, including covenant headroom, retained cash, debt capacity and expected ATM issuance; rerun per-share values if issuance becomes planned, contracted or probable.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: June 30, 2026 retirement-benefit liabilities were $33.8 million, accompanied by $13.7 million of retirement regulatory assets and $6.4 million of SERP-designated marketable securities; the gross liability equals approximately $1.85 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retirement deficit not recoverable through rates or covered by dedicated assets would reduce the bridge or require future cash contributions that reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has recorded on its consolidated balance sheets as a liability the underfunded status of its and its subsidiaries’ retirement benefit obligations based on the projected benefit obligation.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms a claim but also substantial offsets and expected rate recovery. Even deducting the entire $33.8 million gross liability with no credit for regulatory recovery or SERP assets would reduce base value by about $1.85 per share, from negative $5.58 to approximately negative $7.43. That cannot change the present no-buy conclusion relative to the $53.71 market price, although the proper residual should still be documented.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension, PBOP and SERP obligations to plan and trust assets, deferred taxes and jurisdiction-specific regulatory recovery; ensure any residual cash contributions are included once, either in projected OE or the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity may be operationally restricted rather than surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.0 million of the $9.2 million June 30, 2026 cash balance was deposited for ISO-NE assurance, leaving at most $3.2 million before other operating-liquidity requirements; the demonstrated overstatement is approximately $0.33 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding required assurance deposits or operating liquidity as surplus cash overstates the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under this Policy, Unitil’s subsidiaries provide cash deposits covering approximately 2-1/2 months of outstanding obligations, less credit amounts that are based on the Company’s credit rating.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error for at least the $6.0 million ISO-NE deposit. Removing that amount would reduce base value from negative $5.58 to approximately negative $5.91 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion against the $53.71 market price. Other subsidiary or working-liquidity restrictions remain unquantified but cannot exceed the remaining $3.2 million cash balance.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $9.2 million cash balance to the $6.0 million ISO-NE deposit, subsidiary restrictions and minimum operating liquidity, then rerun the bridge using only documented excess cash.
